full_judgment:
6. From Annexure-C it appears that the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate before disposal of the afore-mentioned petition of the Assistant Superintendent of CID called for the opinion of the Public Prosecutor and Public Prosecutor gave his opinion to the effect that there is provision for further investigation under section 5(6) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, that the Special Judge is competent to take cognizance and before or after taking cognizance may pass order for further investigation for ends of justice but in cases where the police is of opinion that further investigation is necessary then as per provisions of section 173(3B) police itself may hold further investigation after submission of the report once and may submit supplementary charge-sheet after such further investigation, that if police take such action at its own initiative then it would not be in contravention of section 5(6) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act Certified copy of that opinion of the public prosecutor has been annexed as Annexure-C(1). 

 9. Me Khan's contention is that in view of this provision of the special law ie Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 neither the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate nor any other court had any jurisdiction to order for further investigation into the case and the order of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate for taking opinion of the PP on the petition of the Assistant Superintendent of Police, CID seeking permission for further investigation and giving of the opinion in writing by the PP and subsequent order of the CMM in this respect were illegal and without jurisdiction and void ab initio and, as such, the supplementary charge sheet submitted by the Assistant Superintendent, CID is illegal and no action can be taken on that basis and therefore the proceeding being the consequences of the supplementary charge sheet is void and not tenable in the eye of law. 

 13. Mr Khan's contention is that in view of the provision of section 5(6) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 in a case under the afore-mentioned Act of 1958 the provisions of section 173(3B) has become negated and once a police report was submitted either in the charge sheet or final report police cannot make further investigation in the case unless there is an order from the Senior Special Judge or Special Judge trying the case. The second contention is that since the case is triable by a Special Judge, the Magistrate had no authority either to obtain opinion of the PP or to direct the CID officer to act in accordance with the advice of the' public prosecutor. 

 15. In that view of the matter, we are of the opinion that the CID committed no error of law in holding further investigation as per provisions of section 173(3B) of the CrPC. Had further investigation been done after the case record was transmitted to the Senior Special Judge after taking cognizance of the offence or passing any order whatsoever then permission of the Special Judge would have been necessary. Further, we also hold that even at that stage the police had the power to hold further investigation as per provision of section 173(3B) of the Code as the provision of this section is in no way derogatory to the provisions of sub-section 5(6) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958. The learned CMM committed no error of law by obtaining the opinion of the PP and by asking the CID Officer to act in accordance with law as per advice of the Public Prosecutor.
